name: Seated calf raise
cue: Sink your heels into a deep stretch, pause, then press up.
research: Seated calf raise on a plate-loaded lever machine. Seated upright, sit bones on the seat (ischia pin), knees 90 deg under a roller pad on the lower thighs just above the kneecaps, hips 90, the balls of the feet on the rear edge of a foot block 18 cm high, heels free, hands on the handles of the lever. With the knee bent ~90 deg the gastrocnemius (it also crosses the knee) is slack, so the soleus does most of the work (Kinoshita et al. 2023, Front Physiol 14:1272106: 12 weeks of seated knee-90 calf raises grew the soleus as much as standing ones but the gastrocnemius hardly at all; ExRx lists the soleus as the target of the lever seated calf raise). Range: the bottom half, after Jeff Nippard (calves respond to a deep stretch: pause in it and do not chase the top): ankle 25 deg dorsiflexion (heels 8 cm below the block top, 7 cm above the base) -> 5 deg plantarflexion, with a 1.5 s pause in the stretch (the app's calf tempo: lift 1.0, top 0.2, lower 2.0, stretch 1.5 s; Kinoshita used 20 deg dorsiflexion -> 30 deg plantarflexion over the full range). Rolling contact: the toe joint (metatarsal-head line) stays on the block edge and the toes stay flat (toe ext = -foot pitch), so the foot rolls about the metatarsal heads; hip and knee angles are solved per key (via keys M1-M5, tools/design/seated_calf_raise.mjs) so the toe joint never leaves its socket: the knees rise 7.6 cm (hip 90 -> 100, knee 90 -> 97.8). Machine: with the pelvis still, the thighs turn about the hip axis as the knees rise, so the roller rides on two side arms hinged on hubs coaxial with the hips (outboard, on posts beside the seat), as the leg-extension hub sits on the knee axis: the lever turns with the thighs (0 -> 10.0 deg, keyed with the hip angle) and the roller never slides on them. Load: plate horns on the arm ends 0.12 H past the roller, in front of the knees (1.6:1, like the 3:1 plate-loaded seated calf machines such as the Body-Solid GSCR349 Kinoshita used), plates outboard; they rise 10 cm with the knees. Muscles: primary soleus (label Calves), secondary gastrocnemius (also Calves, so the chip line reads Calves); the soleus is painted where it is superficial, below and beside the gastrocnemius bellies into the Achilles (head soleus in tools/muscles_src.mjs), so the ember lower calf sits under the amber gastrocnemius heads.

camera.note: Research view: the right profile at calf height (az 90, el 0), square to the sagittal plane of the ankle action. The calves face backward on the vertical shins, so the view turns 28 deg toward the rear and drops 5 deg (az 118, el -5: 28.4 deg in all, inside the 30 deg budget): the posterolateral calves face the camera, the soleus (ember, lower calf) under the gastrocnemius (amber, upper calf) on both legs, and the heels can be seen dropping below the block at the stretch. Fill 0.64: the calves are a small part of a seated figure. The hip-axis hubs, the lever arms and the plates stay above the knees; nothing crosses the calves.

skinChecks.note: forefoot stays on the block through the loop
roller stays on the lower thighs
heels hang free above the base
